  • Question 5. Differentiate between convenience sampling and snowball
  • sampling based on participant recruitment. (2 Marks) [CO3, An]
  • • Convenience Sampling: Participants are recruited solely based on ease of access,
  • geographic proximity, or ready availability to the researcher (e.g., passersby,
  • available volunteers) — 1 mark
  • • Snowball Sampling: Initial identified participants who meet specific research criteria
  • serve as informants to refer, recruit, or nominate subsequent participants from their
  • network (ideal for hidden, hard-to-reach, or specialized populations) — 1 mark
  • Question 6. Mention two characteristics of conceptual research. (2 Marks)
  • [CO1, U]
  • • Focus on ideas and theories: Relies on abstract theories, intellectual concepts, and
  • philosophical frameworks rather than conducting empirical experiments or practical
  • field trials — 1 mark
  • • Re-interpretation and synthesis: Involves critical re-examination, re-interpretation,
  • refinement, or synthesis of existing theories and concepts to develop new conceptual
  • paradigms or models — 1 mark
  • Question 7. Examine the major factors that influence the selection of a
  • sampling design. (2 Marks) [CO3, An]
  • • Nature and structure of the population: Population size, homogeneity vs.
  • heterogeneity, geographic dispersion, and accessibility of a complete sampling frame
  • — 1 mark
  • • Resource constraints and precision: Budget, time limits, available manpower, and the
  • desired level of precision, confidence interval, and acceptable margin of error — 1
  • mark
  • Question 8. What is grouped data? (2 Marks) [CO4, U]
  • • Definition: Raw data that has been organized, aggregated, and classified into
  • mutually exclusive and exhaustive categories, frequency bins, or class intervals — 1
  • mark
  • • Characteristics: Presented as a frequency distribution table to simplify large datasets
  • and reveal underlying patterns, though individual raw data values are condensed — 1
  • mark
  • Question 9. How is coefficient of variation used to compare variability? (2
  • Marks) [CO5, U]
  • • Definition and Formula: Relative measure of dispersion defined as the ratio of
  • standard deviation (σ or s) to the arithmetic mean (μ or x̄), expressed as a
  • percentage: CV = (s / x̄) * 100 — 1 mark
  • • Application: Used to compare the degree of variation, stability, or consistency
  • between two or more datasets measured in different units or having widely different
  • magnitudes of means (lower CV indicates higher consistency/uniformity) — 1 mark
  • Question 10. What is the importance of objectivity in research? (2 Marks) [CO1,
  • K]
  • • Elimination of bias: Ensures that observations, data collection, analytical findings, and
  • conclusions are free from personal prejudice, value judgments, investigator
  • expectations, and emotional bias — 1 mark
  • • Scientific validity and reproducibility: Enhances scientific credibility, transparency,
  • universal acceptance, and reproducibility by other independent researchers across
  • the global scientific community — 1 mark
  • Question 11. Differentiate between population and unit of analysis with a
  • suitable example. (2 Marks) [CO3, An]
  • • Distinction: 'Population' is the entire aggregated pool or universe of cases/elements
  • that possess specific characteristics of interest. 'Unit of analysis' is the specific
  • individual entity, subject, or object being directly analyzed and measured within that
  • study — 1 mark
  • • Illustrative Example: In a study assessing bloodstain pattern analysis in homicides
  • across Kerala: Population = All registered homicide crime scenes in Kerala; Unit of
  • analysis = An individual bloodstain pattern / individual crime scene docket — 1 mark
  • Question 12. Explain a discrete variable with an example. (2 Marks) [CO4, U]
  • • Definition: A quantitative variable that can only assume distinct, separate, countable
  • values with no intermediate fractional values between adjacent points (takes isolated
  • integer values) — 1 mark
  • • Example: Number of bullet cartridges recovered from a crime scene, number of ridge
  • bifurcations in a fingerprint, number of PCR amplification cycles (accept any valid
  • countable example) — 1 mark

questions.question: Explain the major steps involved in conducting analytical research. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
Step-by-Step Valuation Scheme:

2. Analytical Development & Proof Steps (2.0 Marks): Rigorous derivation, systematic reasoning, and logical progression.
3. Synthesized Conclusion & Interpretation (2.0 Marks): Final formulated result, physical/academic significance, and domain limitations.
